neighbours.label: A token inside a hypothetical counterexample that shows a measure misleads (a society where everyone is equally poor would score as equal; heavy boats have a messy wake even at speed)
fire: Average income is a poor guide; a town where everyone earns the same low wage would look perfectly fair.
Speed is not a reliable sign of skill; some reckless drivers have fast lap times even in the rain.
GDP misses a lot; a country where everyone works double shifts would look richer than it feels.
Height is a weak proxy for age; some young trees have tall trunks even in poor soil.
Test scores can mislead; a school where every pupil is coached for the exam would rank near the top.
Price is not a good measure of quality; some cheap wines have rich flavor even without aging.
Turnout alone says little; a country where voting is compulsory would always look engaged.
Weight is a poor sign of health; some heavy athletes have very low body fat even in the off season.
quiet: Average income in the town rose last year as new factories opened.
Speed on the track improved after the team changed the tires.
GDP in the country grew by two percent over the last quarter.
Height of the trees was measured every spring by the rangers.
Test scores at the school went up after the new teacher arrived.
Price of the wine dropped after the harvest was larger than expected.
Turnout in the election was higher than in the previous one.
Weight of the athletes was recorded before each training session.

predictions: Counterexample clauses after 'X is a poor measure' 0.3-0.7; the same topics stated plainly under 0.1. May fail: only 2 of 5 probe frames fired.
notes: Card: peaks on ' where', ' have', ' and', ' even', ' both', ' only' inside critiques of a measure. Probe: 'a society where everyone is equally poor would' 0.731, 'messy wake even at speed' 0.553; but 'add jobs and not see unemployment fall' 0.135, 'even though they rated teachers poorly' 0.023, 'searched only once' 0.151; plain controls 0.004-0.015.
